newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH stock looks good to many analysts.
newsitem.headline: LVMH stock looks good to many analysts.

text.p: Lehman Brothers cut its rating on Tuesday on the blue-chip stock of acquisitive luxury goods group LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton, but other analysts said they remained bullish on the share.

"The tone of positive press comment surrounding the company has all the hallmarks of a bubble about to burst," Lehman analyst John Wakely wrote in a comment explaining his move to lower the rating on LVMH stock to underperform from neutral.
"Though we shy away from making value judgments, 30 times 1997 earnings and 20 times cashflow in our experience is only matched by Coca-Cola," Wakely said.
He said LVMH did not appear to have have got a good price for the seven percent of Guinness Plc that it sold at 414 pence last week.
LVMH said part of the five billion francs ($913 million) in proceeds would help finance the $2.47 billion acquisition of U.S. duty free chain DFS concluded earlier this month.

"These actions show the new orientation of the company's portfolio toward luxury goods and retailing through DFS. Even if the profile is more risky, the long-term growth outlook is better," said a Paris analyst, who values the share at between 1,500 and 1,600 francs.

LVMH's stock was trading 1.67 percent lower at 1,470 francs at 1135 GMT. Over the past 12 months it has gained 44 percent, outperforming the bourse's CAC-40 index which has risen just over 25 percent in the same period.
"I still remain a solid buy on the LVMH despite the good share run," said Cedric Magnelia at CS First Boston.

"DFS is strategically and financially a sound acquisition. We believe in continued volume growth at Louis Vuitton," the designer luggage branch with the biggest profit margin in the group, he said. He added that foreign exchange movements, particularly the dollar's rise, were favourable for LVMH.

Analyst Cecile d'Estais at Paribas Capital Markets said she believed LVMH shares would continue to outperform the bourse, which is expected to keep rising from current near-record levels. Her 12-month target for the share is 1,600 francs.

Another Paris brokerage issued a note on Monday raising its objective for the stock to 1,880 francs over the next 12 months from 1,570 francs previously, citing gains in profitability expected to result from LVMH's acquisition of DFS.
LVMH has said the acquisition would boost sales by around 50 percent and operating profit by nearly a third.
A Paris-based analyst who spoke on condition of anonymity said the purchase of San Francisco-based DFS, which has 180 shops along the Pacific Rim, was strategically positive.
"For a long time the motor for the company was Japan, and that motor is slowing down," he said. "This brings them closer to new Southeast Asian clientele."

Analysts are watching to see whether LVMH will buy the remainder of DFS -- 38.75 percent owner Robert Miller is still resisting the deal -- or sell more of its remaining 14 percent Guinness stake. One analyst said the operations might roughly offset each other in terms of impact on profit.
-- Christine Tierney, Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.474 French Francs)
